To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perceived sincerity of a collective apology is a function of representativeness of the apology for the offender group's will or sentiment, which is affected by the degree of intragroup agreement and subtyping within the offender group.
the perceived sincerity of a group apology depends on its representativeness for a group’s sentiment and that the perceived representativeness of a group apology is affected by intragroup processes.
the sincerity of an apology for a collective offense is a function of its perceived representatiness for the offender group's will or sentiment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of who speaks for the offender group in a collective apology.
the role of representativeness in the perception of apology sincerity and the consequences for intergroup forgiveness.
the question of how victims judge the representativeness of apologies in intergroup conflict and how this influences their willingness to forgive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
apology representativeness determines the sincerity of a collective apology.
the sincerity of a collective apology is determined by the representativeness of the apology for the will and sentiment of the offending group.
the perceived sincerity of an apology for a collective wrongdoing is a function of its representativeness for its offending group’s will or sentiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perceived representativeness of an apology for the offender group's will or sentiment, rather than its accuracy, is critical for it to lead to victim forgiveness.
the representativeness of an apology for the will of the offending out-group is a crucial determinant of its perceived sincerity and, thus, of its ability to promote forgiveness.
the perceived representativeness of an apology is a key determinant of its perceived sincerity in intergroup contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in intergroup contexts, the representativeness of an apology for the offending group’s will matters for its perceived sincerity and forgiveness.
apology representativeness is critical in determining whether an apology is viewed positively by its recipients.
the perceived sincerity of a collective apology depends on how representative it is of the offending out-group’s will.
